title: Total Quality Management (TQM)
subject: Project quality management
description: Twenty-five questions across easy, medium and hard on TQM in project management: its principles, life cycle application, tools and how it differs from quality control.

questions.prompt: What is Total Quality Management (TQM)?
options: A set of tests carried out on finished deliverables
A standard for auditing management systems
A tool for ranking defects by frequency
A management approach focused on continuous improvement, customer satisfaction, employee involvement and error prevention
questions.explanation: TQM is a broad management approach rather than a single tool or test.

questions.prompt: As applied to project management, what does TQM ensure?
options: That activities, processes, materials, services and deliverables meet established quality standards and satisfy stakeholders
That the project finishes early whatever the cost
That only the final deliverable is inspected
That quality duties rest with a single inspector
questions.explanation: TQM covers the whole project, not just the final product.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an objective of TQM in project management?
options: Replace quality standards with client preferences
Increase inspection at the end of the project
Reduce project costs by minimising waste, rework and defects
Limit teamwork to the quality department
questions.explanation: TQM aims to reduce waste, rework, defects and unnecessary expenditure, and it encourages teamwork across the project.

questions.prompt: What does the customer focus principle say?
options: Project decisions should be guided mainly by the lowest cost
Project decisions should be guided by the needs and expectations of the client and other relevant stakeholders
Only the project manager should communicate with the client
Client feedback is needed only after handover
questions.explanation: Customer focus keeps decisions tied to what the client and stakeholders need.

questions.prompt: Which project phase includes obtaining client acceptance, documenting lessons learned and completing handover?
options: Project initiation
Project planning
Project execution
Project closure
questions.explanation: At closure the team verifies deliverables, corrects defects, obtains client acceptance, records lessons learned and completes handover.

questions.prompt: What does PDCA stand for?
options: Plan, Do, Check, Act
Prepare, Deliver, Control, Approve
Plan, Direct, Confirm, Assess
Prevent, Detect, Correct, Audit
questions.explanation: PDCA is a cycle for improvement: identify a problem, implement a solution, evaluate the results, then standardise or revise.

questions.prompt: What does Pareto analysis do in TQM?
options: Records every observation on a prepared form
Helps prioritise the few causes responsible for a large share of defects or problems
Verifies compliance with contract terms
Shows the sequence of steps in a process
questions.explanation: Pareto analysis focuses effort on the small number of causes behind most problems.

questions.prompt: What is the central idea of TQM stated in the conclusion?
options: Quality is best ensured by a single final inspection
Quality matters mainly in construction projects
Quality should be built in from the beginning and continuously improved, not only inspected at the end
Quality improvement stops once execution begins
questions.explanation: TQM integrates quality into every stage of project delivery.

questions.prompt: What does the employee involvement principle require?
options: Every team member takes responsibility for quality within their assigned duties
Only supervisors are responsible for quality
Quality is left entirely to designated inspectors
Employees take part only in the final review
questions.explanation: Quality is everyone's responsibility under TQM.

questions.prompt: What should project leaders do under the leadership commitment principle?
options: Delegate all quality decisions to suppliers
Establish quality objectives, provide resources and demonstrate commitment to quality standards
Inspect every deliverable personally
Leave quality objectives for the client to set
questions.explanation: Leaders set the direction and provide the means, and they show commitment by their own actions.

questions.prompt: What does the process approach mean in TQM?
options: Each activity is managed separately with no link to the others
Only the final output is measured against standards
Procedures are written only after defects appear
Project activities are organised and managed as interconnected processes with clear procedures and performance standards
questions.explanation: Seeing the work as linked processes makes it easier to define procedures, set standards and find where problems arise.

questions.prompt: A manager insists on deciding from reliable data instead of opinion. Which TQM principle is this?
options: Leadership commitment
Employee involvement
Evidence-based decision-making
Relationship management
questions.explanation: Decisions should rest on reliable data, quality inspections, measurements and performance indicators.

questions.prompt: Why does TQM stress good relationships with suppliers, contractors and consultants?
options: Effective relationships help maintain consistent quality
They allow the project to transfer all quality responsibility to them
They remove the need to inspect their work
They make a quality plan unnecessary
questions.explanation: These parties affect the quality of what the project delivers, so working well with them supports consistent quality.

questions.prompt: Which TQM activities belong to project execution?
options: Identify client expectations and define quality objectives
Implement approved procedures, train workers, supervise activities and control processes
Prepare the quality plan and inspection procedures
Verify deliverables and obtain client acceptance
questions.explanation: The other options belong to initiation, planning and closure.

questions.prompt: Which pairing correctly places TQM activities in the project life cycle?
options: Initiation: prepare the quality plan; planning: identify client expectations
Initiation: conduct audits and tests; planning: hand over the project
Initiation: train workers; planning: obtain client acceptance
Initiation: identify client expectations and define quality objectives; planning: prepare the quality plan, specifications and inspection procedures
questions.explanation: TQM begins with understanding client expectations and then turns them into a plan, standards and procedures.

questions.prompt: What happens during project monitoring and control under TQM?
options: Client expectations are identified for the first time
Lessons learned are documented and the project is handed over
Inspections, audits, testing and performance measurements are used to identify deviations
Quality standards are selected for the first time
questions.explanation: Monitoring and control compares actual performance with what was planned so deviations can be found.

questions.prompt: What does statistical process control do?
options: Uses measurements and control charts to monitor process variation and identify unusual changes
Lists items to verify before work proceeds
Ranks causes by their share of defects
Records lessons from project reviews
questions.explanation: Statistical process control watches how a process varies over time so unusual changes are noticed.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts TQM with project quality control (PQC)?
options: TQM is a set of checking activities, while PQC is a management philosophy
TQM emphasises detecting defects, while PQC emphasises prevention
TQM focuses on verifying outputs, while PQC focuses on long-term culture
TQM is a wider management philosophy emphasising prevention and improvement, while PQC is a set of checking activities emphasising inspection and testing
questions.explanation: TQM focuses on a long-term quality culture and stakeholder satisfaction, while PQC verifies that outputs meet acceptance criteria.

questions.prompt: On a lecture hall project, inspections reveal cracked concrete. Which TQM response does the lecture give?
options: Fill the cracks and continue to protect the schedule
Investigate root causes, verify the concrete mix, and improve curing and inspection procedures
Add more workers to speed up the casting
Change suppliers before checking the cause
questions.explanation: TQM looks for the root cause and fixes the process, not only the visible symptom.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of problem and TQM response is correct?
options: Delayed deliveries: inspect materials before acceptance
Poor-quality materials: improve curing procedures
Repeated rework: train workers, improve work procedures and prevent defects before later activities begin
Client dissatisfaction: monitor procurement performance
questions.explanation: Poor materials call for supplier evaluation and inspection, delayed deliveries for better supplier coordination, and client dissatisfaction for feedback and verification against agreed specifications.

questions.prompt: What results does the lecture expect from applying TQM in the lecture hall case?
options: Fewer defects but higher rework costs because of extra inspection
Reduced defects, lower rework costs, improved schedule performance and greater client satisfaction
A faster schedule at the cost of client satisfaction
Fewer inspections and no need for supplier checks
questions.explanation: Building quality into the process cuts defects and rework, which helps schedule and the client's confidence.

questions.prompt: An inspector suspects a structural defect in a concrete element. According to the lecture, what must happen before the work is accepted or concealed?
options: Qualified professionals must assess it
The contractor may certify it informally
Finishes may be applied once the cracks look minor
The project manager alone may approve it quickly
questions.explanation: The lecture stresses that suspected structural defects must be assessed by qualified professionals before the affected work is accepted or concealed.

questions.prompt: A team lacks reliable defect records and cannot measure how its processes are performing. Which challenge of TQM does this reflect?
options: Resistance to organisational change
Insufficient employee training
Pressure to complete projects quickly
Inadequate quality data and monitoring systems
questions.explanation: The lecture says such challenges can be addressed through leadership commitment, staff training, effective communication, realistic project planning and regular performance reviews.

questions.prompt: Which statement about who is involved in TQM and PQC is correct?
options: TQM is carried out only by inspectors, while PQC involves everyone
Both are carried out only by the quality manager
TQM involves everyone responsible for project processes, while PQC is often carried out by designated inspectors and testers, with wider team involvement as needed
TQM involves only senior managers, while PQC involves only suppliers
questions.explanation: TQM spreads responsibility for quality across the whole team. PQC is more specialised.

questions.prompt: How does quality control relate to TQM?
options: Quality control replaces TQM once a project begins
TQM is one narrow part of quality control
The two approaches are unrelated
Quality control is one component of effective project quality management, while TQM is a broader approach to managing and improving quality
questions.explanation: Quality control checks outputs, and TQM is the wider approach in which that checking takes place.
